header.title: Blocklist control
header.desc: Maintain blocklists and policy groups, published to the resolver via RPZ to block domains and answer IPs.

listCard.title: Blocklist library
listCard.hint: Feeds sync every 30 seconds · the previous version is kept on failure

list.empty: No blocklist yet. Click New blocklist in the top right to create one
list.deleteDesc: The list and all its entries will be deleted permanently.

blocklist.note: Built-in lists cannot be deleted; feed syncs save a version snapshot first, so any version can be rolled back with one click;  the block page text and IP are configured under Security & diagnostics.

pg.title: Policy groups
pg.empty: No policy group yet. Click Create group to apply RPZ per view

createModal.hint: Feeds are checked every 30 seconds; the previous version is kept if sync fails. Add entries to the list after creating it.

pgModal.title: New policy group
pgModal.hint: View names are unique per resolver; the allowlist takes precedence over the blocklist. An empty time window means all day; start > end means crossing midnight (e.g. 22:00→06:00) and blocking is lifted outside the window.

entries.title: List entries
entries.empty: This list has no entries yet. Use the form above to add the first rule.

csv.title: Import blocklist entries from CSV
csv.hint: Clear the existing entries of this list before importing (a version snapshot is saved first, so it can be rolled back)

versions.title: Snapshots and rollback
versions.empty: No snapshot yet: one is saved automatically before feed syncs and CSV imports
versions.rollbackDesc: Current entries will be replaced by the snapshot content; the version number keeps increasing.

builtin.note: Built-in packs are baseline seeds (not exhaustive). Once installed they become builtin lists that you can extend, trim or combine with feeds.

msg.feedUrlRequired: A feed URL is required for feed lists
msg.rollbackOk: Rolled back to v{version} (the version number keeps increasing)

header.title: DNS records
header.desc: Maintain A / AAAA / CNAME / PTR / TXT / SRV / MX records per zone and review records derived automatically by DHCP dual-stack linkage.

stat.linkedHintOn: Derived automatically by DHCP dual-stack linkage

zoneCard.title: DNS zones
zoneCard.emptyDescNoZone: Click New zone in the top right to create the first authoritative or local zone
zoneCard.emptyDescNoMatch: Adjust the keyword or status filter

recordCard.title: DNS records
recordCard.emptyNoRecords: This zone has no records yet. Click Add record to create one

linked.hint: Read-only · maintained by DHCP dual-stack linkage
linked.note: Linked records are generated automatically by DHCP dual-stack linkage: when a client obtains an address via DHCP, the control plane derives A / AAAA records from the hostname and IP and keeps them in sync with the lease. This view is read-only; change the hostname or binding on the DHCP side.
linked.emptyNoRecords: This zone has no linked records

emptyNoZone.title: No zone selected yet
emptyNoZone.desc: Pick a zone on the left to view its records, or click New zone to create one

addModal.nameHint: Wildcards are only allowed as the leftmost label (*.example.com); a lone * means a zone-apex wildcard
addModal.valuePlaceholder: IP for A/AAAA; domain (with trailing dot) for CNAME/PTR
addModal.hint: Records resolve immediately after creation; static records win over linked records on conflict.

editModal.nameHint: Wildcards are only allowed as the leftmost label (*.example.com)

zoneModal.hint: Authoritative zones answer external queries; local zones only serve intranet clients; secondary zones sync from the primary via AXFR (local zone records are read-only and maintained by the primary). A trailing dot is appended on save.

hosts.title: Import hosts
hosts.hint: Creates one A/AAAA record per name (TTL 300); duplicates are skipped automatically; the zonefile is re-rendered after import.

msg.warnNoZone: Select or create a zone first
msg.warnNameValue: Enter the record name and value
msg.deleteContent: The {name} {type} record under {zone} will be deleted.
msg.zoneDeleteContent: All records under it will be deleted and removed from the resolver configuration.

header.title: Upstream DNS servers
header.desc: Maintain the upstream servers and protocols used for recursion; unhealthy nodes are removed automatically based on health probes.

stat.rttHintOff: Waiting for the first probe result

toolbar.hint: Removed upstreams are excluded from recursion

upstream.empty: No upstream server yet. Click Add upstream in the top right to create one

msg.warnAddr: Enter at least one upstream address
msg.updated: Upstream updated and delivered to the resolver

form.tlsHint: Upstream hostname used for certificate validation; leave empty to connect by address (some upstreams reject this)
form.addrPlaceholder: Multiple values allowed, comma separated, e.g. 223.5.5.5:53,223.6.6.6:53
form.hintWeight: Higher weight means a higher chance of being selected; DoT renders as
form.hintTail: , default port 853. When DoT and plaintext upstreams are mixed, only the DoT target is used (to avoid plaintext fallback).

header.title: Security & diagnostics
header.desc: Configure response rate limiting, DNSSEC validation and transport policy, then verify real query results with the test console.

stat.rrlHintOn: Answers from over-limit sources are dropped
stat.rrlHintOff: Leaving it off exposes you to amplification attacks
stat.rateHintOn: Per-second quota calculated per source IP
stat.rateHintOff: Configurable once rate limiting is on
stat.dnssecHintOn: Validates the signature chain and rejects tampered answers
stat.lastHintOff: Run a query in the console below

policy.title: Security policy
policy.hint: Takes effect after the resolver configuration reloads

form.rateHint: Per-second answer quota calculated per source IP
form.tcpHintOn: UDP queries return truncated answers, forcing a TCP retry
form.tcpHintOff: Both UDP and TCP are served
form.hint: Source IPs over the limit have their answers dropped (matching the resolver's official ip-ratelimit semantics); TCP-only responses add latency for some legacy clients.

blockPage.label: Block page
blockPage.hint: redirect blocklist entries resolve to the IP below and browsers show an explanation page;  leave it empty to treat redirect entries as NXDOMAIN.
blockPage.msgPlaceholder: This domain is blocked by network usage policy. Please contact your network administrator.

loading.title: Loading security settings
loading.desc: If this takes too long, check control plane connectivity and retry

test.title: Resolution test console
test.hint: dig-style live query · simulate a source IP to hit a view
test.clientPlaceholder: Optional, used to verify view matching
test.emptyAnswersDesc: Response code {rcode}; the domain may not exist, may be blocked, or the upstream may have timed out
test.emptyDesc: Enter a domain and type, then click Query to see the response code, latency, view and answers

header.title: Cache & performance
header.desc: Tune the resolver cache TTL, stale-answer fallback and per-domain overrides, and review query volume.

stat.peakHintOn: Highest hourly volume in the window
stat.coversHintOn: Per-domain overrides take precedence over the global TTL

card.hint: Takes effect after the resolver configuration reloads

form.minHint: 0 means unlimited; cache using the response TTL
form.maxHint: Response TTLs above this value are truncated to it
form.serveExpiredOn: Serve stale cache when the upstream times out

loading.title: Loading settings
loading.desc: If this takes too long, check control plane connectivity and retry

flush.title: Flush cache manually
flush.zonePlaceholder: Leave empty to flush the whole cache
flush.confirmDescZone: Cache entries for {zone} will be flushed.
flush.confirmDescAll: The whole cache will be flushed, which may cause a short burst of upstream traffic.
flush.hint: The first query after flushing goes back to the upstream

ttl.title: Per-domain TTL overrides
ttl.hint: Takes precedence over the global cache TTL
ttl.toolbarHint: Submitting the same domain again overwrites the previous value
ttl.emptyDesc: Set a shorter TTL for frequently updated domains using the form above

msg.saved: Settings saved and applied via checkconf-reload

header.title: Conditional forwarding rules
header.desc: Forward queries to a specific upstream by domain suffix. The longest suffix wins; unmatched queries fall back to the default upstream.

stat.enabledHint: {n} disabled rules are excluded from selection
stat.defaultsHintOn: The root domain dot catches all unmatched queries
stat.defaultsHintOff: No default forward configured, recursion is used

card.title: Forwarding rules
card.hint: Queries matching no rule use the default upstream

toolbar.hint: A trailing dot is appended on save

forward.empty: No forwarding rule yet. Click Add forwarding rule in the top right to create one
forward.note: Rules are matched by suffix length in descending order; only one rule per suffix is kept, and editing only allows changing the upstream and note.

msg.warnRequired: Domain suffix and forwarding upstream are required

form.domainPlaceholder: e.g. corp.local (the longest suffix wins; use . for the default)
form.notePlaceholder: Optional, describe the purpose of this suffix
form.hint: A trailing dot is appended to build the FQDN; the rule is delivered to the resolver immediately after saving.
